name: Georgia
permitAge: 15 (Class CP instructional permit), after vision and knowledge exams; parent, guardian or responsible adult signs; proof of school enrollment under 18 (handbook p. 8)

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours, including 6 at night (Joshua's Law); DDS affidavit at the road test, parent or guardian attests, no logbook (handbook p. 8; dds.georgia.gov/joshuas-law-requirements)
teen.holdPermit: 1 year and 1 day before the Class D license at 16 (handbook p. 8)
teen.nightLimit: Class D: no driving 12:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m., no exceptions (handbook pp. 8, 27)
teen.passengerLimit: Class D: first 6 months only immediate family; second 6 months at most one non-family passenger under 21; after that at most three non-family passengers under 21 (handbook pp. 8, 27)
teen.phone: All drivers: Hands Free Georgia Law (HB 673, O.C.G.A. 40-6-241(c), 2018): may not hold or support a phone; use only with headphones, wireless device, holder or mount (handbook p. 25)

notes: Handbook: Georgia Drivers Manual 2023-2024 (DDS), scanned PDF (metadata modified June 2023); the HTML manual at dds.georgia.gov/drivers-manual has the same text. Page numbers are the printed ones (printed page 7 is missing from the PDF scan).

Knowledge exam: two tests, Road Signs and Road Rules, 20 questions each, 15 correct needed on each (handbook p. 12; DDS test page). Stored as 40 questions, 30 to pass, but each part must be passed separately.

Test languages: the handbook (p. 12) says the signs test is English only; the newer DDS test page (checked 2026-10-09) says both parts are offered in 26 languages, including Spanish, Chinese, Vietnamese, Arabic and Haitian Creole (not Tagalog). The road skills test is English only.
Learner's permit supervisor: at least 21, licensed to drive a Class C vehicle, fit to take control, in the seat beside the driver (handbook p. 8).
Joshua's Law: 30-hour approved course (classroom or online) plus 6 hours with a certified instructor or the DDS Parent/Teen Driving Guide; 40 supervised hours, 6 at night (handbook p. 8).
School bus: all traffic stops, except opposite-direction traffic on a highway divided by a median (handbook pp. 18, 44).
Move Over Law: move over one lane when safe; otherwise slow below the limit and be prepared to stop (handbook p. 18). A later change to the law was not checked.
No official Spanish driver manual found on the DDS manuals page (2026-10-09).
